name: Kolkar clan
summary: Across Kalimdor, the Kolkar clan raids settlements and turns on all who cross its path. The red-marked centaur claim descent from the first Khan, Kolk, and hold strongholds in Desolace and the Barrens.

sections.title: Sons of Kolk
sections.body: The Kolkar take their name from Khan Kolk, the first centaur khan. He was born from the union of Zaetar and Theradras. The clan hates other races and its fellow centaur clans, and its red markings set it apart. The Kolkar refuse all alliances. Their ancient village stood in eastern Desolace, where Khan Kolk's restless spirit still wanders beneath their ancestral lands.

sections.title: The Scourge of the Barrens
sections.body: For generations, Kolkar raids harried the nomadic tauren crossing the arid Barrens. During the Third War, the orcs came to Kalimdor. Thrall joined Cairne Bloodhoof to drive the marauding centaur back and escort the tauren to safety in Mulgore. Defeat only deepened the feud. The Kolkar entrenched themselves around the Barrens' three vital water sources: the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater Oasis, and the Stagnant Oasis.

sections.title: Encroachment on Durotar
sections.body: From fortified positions across the savanna, the Kolkar have pushed east past the Southfury River into Durotar. At Kolkar Crag in the south, raiding parties plot assaults on Sen'jin Village, the Valley of Trials, and the paths toward Orgrimmar. Senior Horde leaders face larger regional threats, so young recruits are sent to curb the centaur advance before its raiders strike the young orc capital.

faq.answer: The Kolkar are one of Kalimdor's five major centaur clans. Named for their first leader, Khan Kolk, they are fierce and xenophobic, marked by red armor. They keep settlements in Desolace, control the Barrens' main water oases, and maintain raiding camps in southern Durotar.

faq.q: Why do the Kolkar hate the Horde so much?
faq.answer: For generations, the Kolkar hunted and harried the tauren across the Barrens. When Thrall's Horde arrived, the orcs joined Cairne Bloodhoof to drive the centaur back and help the tauren settle in Mulgore. The Kolkar Khans were humiliated, and their long hunt became a bitter war against both orcs and tauren.

faq.q: Why are the Kolkar occupying the Barrens oases?
faq.answer: The Kolkar hold the Barrens' oases because water means survival in that arid land. Command tents, tribal totems, and hyena packs guard the Forgotten Pools, Lushwater Oasis, and Stagnant Oasis, keeping travelers, merchants, and the Horde from these watering holes.

Khan Kolk was the clan's first ruler, and his spirit lingers in Maraudon. In recent times, Khan Dez'hepah and his officers led the clan from the ancient Kolkar Village in Desolace, while Barrens camps answered to leaders such as Hezrul Bloodmark. Other khans, including the fallen Khan Gragtor, led warbands farther afield.

Kolkar Crag is a rocky canyon outpost in southern Durotar. Centaur warbands use it as a forward staging ground to harass Horde initiates in the Valley of Trials, menace Sen'jin Village, and test Orgrimmar's defenses.

faq.q: Do the Kolkar work with other centaur clans?
faq.answer: No. The Kolkar have no kinship or treaties with the other four centaur clans native to Desolace. Centaur society is violently divided, and the Kolkar fight other clans as readily as they fight the Horde and Alliance.

angles.text: Across the Barrens, the Kolkar hunted your people nearly to extinction before the orcs intervened. Each encounter with them touches the survival of your ancestors.
Your first pact with the tauren was forged in blood against Kolkar marauders. Their scouts at Kolkar Crag now threaten the Valley of Trials, where young orcs come of age.
Kolkar control of the three Barrens oases cuts off vital trade and water supplies between Durotar, Mulgore, and the Crossroads.
Kolkar raiding parties rely on trained, partly domesticated hyenas to track intruders and guard the edges of their watering holes.
